title: GW150914 / LIGO gravitational-wave detection: surviving-anomaly positive control for anomaly discipline
summary: A control/calibration record for MKH-PAT-0017. GW150914 prevents the anomaly lane from becoming a debunking lane: an extraordinary signal can survive detector coincidence, statistical testing, source modeling, open data release, and later reanalysis, while still exposing reproducibility and workflow-opacity limits.

status_history.note: MKH-PAT-0017 explicitly needed a surviving-anomaly positive control.
Promoted as first surviving-anomaly positive control for anomaly discipline.

place.scope: LIGO Hanford and LIGO Livingston gravitational-wave detector network; GW150914 event data and reanalysis surface

subjects.name: LIGO Scientific Collaboration and Virgo Collaboration

claims.claim: The GW150914 discovery-paper record reports that on 14 September 2015 the two LIGO detectors simultaneously observed a transient gravitational-wave signal, with matched-filter SNR 24, an estimated false-alarm rate below one event per 203,000 years, and first-direct-detection language.
what_would_change_status: A corrected discovery-paper record or later collaboration correction materially changes the two-detector/SNR/false-alarm/direct-detection characterization.

claims.claim: The official LIGO announcement says the signal was detected by both widely separated LIGO detectors, gives the Hanford/Livingston observatory context, and states that independent widely separated observatories are needed to verify a signal is from space and not a local phenomenon.
what_would_change_status: A stronger source shows the press-release network-control characterization is materially wrong or misleading.

claims.claim: GWOSC released a dedicated GW150914 event-data page with a dataset DOI and data around the event, including strain data in multiple formats and sampling rates, which made external analysis and teaching/reanalysis possible.
what_would_change_status: A GWOSC correction changes the DOI or data-release availability status for GW150914.

claims.claim: Brown et al. report that they could reproduce the main GW150914 discovery-paper result with publicly available code/workflows, but could not exactly reproduce the original LIGO analysis because the original dataset was not public; this makes GW150914 both a positive control and a workflow-transparency caution.
what_would_change_status: A second-pass paper review shows Brown et al. did exact reproduction, or that the original dataset availability statement was misread.

claims.claim: As a control record, GW150914 calibrates MKH-PAT-0017 by showing that anomaly discipline must include surviving anomalies, not only instrument-error, foreground-error, or replication-failure cases. It does not by itself mature the pattern.
what_would_change_status: A future red-team pass shows GW150914 is misclassified as a control or the pattern has been split into a different anomaly-control family.

evidence_refs.support_type: control role and anomaly-discipline calibration encoded in this record
positive control relation to anomaly-discipline candidate

evidence_profile.source_depth: one-pass discovery paper / official release / open-data / reproducibility audit extraction
limitations: Does not re-run LIGO workflows or independently verify data products.
Does not adjudicate all later critiques of GW150914; only encodes a bounded positive-control role for the cube.

type_payload.fit_rationale: GW150914 is an extraordinary physical-science signal that survived network detection, statistical significance, source modeling, data release, and later reanalysis; it prevents anomaly-discipline synthesis from overfitting to false alarms and corrected errors.
limits: Positive control does not mature MKH-PAT-0017.
Open data and public code do not guarantee exact reproduction of the original internal workflow.
Control record is not a full GW150914 technical monograph.

handling_notes: Avoid heroic simplification; the control is about disciplined epistemic process.
Avoid using GW150914 to imply every extraordinary anomaly should be believed.

unknowns: No full second-pass extraction of all companion papers, calibration papers, or detector-characterization papers yet.
No direct code/data execution or independent statistical validation performed inside the cube.
next_actions: Add a second positive-control anomaly outside gravitational-wave physics.
